PHASE 1 RCA (2026-08-14)

Observed problem: organic Verify run 31846417650 emitted 260 fixture_setup spans >1s totaling 380.393 aggregate worker-seconds. The top five module totals were 103.416 worker-seconds. Fresh serial main baselines confirmed setup, not test-call work, dominates the named fixtures: secret-screen 36 passed/19.99s with ~17s setup; list-filters 17 passed/23.54s with 1.02-2.39s setup each; b636 7 passed/11.37s with 1.29-1.58s setup each; backup 12 passed/14.74s with 0.55-0.98s setup each; inline-push 10 passed/9.64s with 0.42-0.79s setup each.

Proven mechanisms and discriminating runtime evidence:
1. tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py:108-120 rebuilds an equivalent virgin store for every consumer. cProfile of two consumers observed two init_repo calls and 99 subprocesses; init_repo consumed 0.919s. A real store built in 0.426s, while three isolated copies took 0.034-0.037s each (~12x); a ticket written in copy A was absent from copy B/template, and identities/worktree refs were disjoint. Secret-screen call behavior cannot explain setup spans.
2. tests/interfaces/queries/test_list_filters.py:57-90 rebuilds the same 11-ticket/claim/transition/delete/link graph for every test. Two consumers observed 22 create_ticket calls and 192 subprocesses. One population took 1.118s versus 0.126s for two isolated copies (~17.7x per copy); exact IDs/statuses matched, and closing BLK in copy A left copy B/template open. CLI call work is timed separately.
3. tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py:255-283 rebuilds the same bare-remote/A/B/shared-ticket topology for every b636 test. The real topology built in 1.445s versus 0.062s to relocate a complete copy (~23x). Every embedded source path was rewritten, git fsck passed on remote/A/B/both trackers, origin URLs pointed into the copy, linked worktrees were self-contained, object inodes were unshared, the seed was visible, and a copy-only ref did not reach the template. b636 call bodies remain real.
4. tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py:85-142 rebuilds a fixed branch/tag/blob/bare-remote graph. The real graph built in 0.635s versus 0.046s per copy (~13.8x); all OID relationships and remote snapshot matched, no source path remained, and a copy-only ref did not reach the template. Bundle/verification call work remains real.
5. tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py:32-46 rebuilds a bare origin plus initialized linked-worktree store. The real topology built in 0.487s versus 0.031s per relocated copy (~15.7x); origin/worktree paths were repaired, identity reminted, a real copy write pushed only to the copy origin, and the template origin stayed unchanged.

Root cause: these function-scoped fixtures execute invariant git/rebar topology construction once per consumer even though the asserted behavior begins after setup. The changeable artifacts are the five fixture scopes/builders above. This is a test-infrastructure defect against the explicit no-coverage-loss runtime goal, not a request to sample or remove coverage. Initialization/recovery contracts remain from-scratch.

OSS/tracker legitimacy: consensus is 3/3. Django 3436cf9 uses setUpTestData plus deep-copy/per-test transaction rollback; Rails 62b5458 loads fixtures once plus per-test rollback/cache invalidation; GitLab dff4132 recommends let_it_be plus rollback/reload and prepared repository bundles, with explicit fallback for migration/delete tests. pytest 68308aa additionally recommends tmp_path_factory session fixtures for expensive generated assets. All were active 2026-08-14; popularity recorded in the investigation (Django 88.4k GitHub stars, Rails 58.7k, GitLab 6.1k stars/12.3k forks). None rejects isolated reuse; each retains from-scratch paths where rollback/copy is not faithful. Closed peculiar-calmy-bubblefish accepted this exact pattern and measured 270.7s -> 186.5s (31%) with nine more tests; adored-duskish-kissingbug strengthened virgin-template assertions. No rejection found.

Caller-dependency gate: expected post-fix behavior is byte/state-equivalent isolated fixture topology with fewer invariant setup subprocesses. All callers are the named tests/fixture consumers. No caller depends on fresh timestamps/UUIDs or shared refs; the experiments preserved recorded OIDs/IDs where contractual and reminted only per-environment identity. Direct initialization/recovery tests are excluded and stay from-scratch. No behavioral dependency blocks Phase 2.

Phase 1 exit: confirmed, cited, parsimonious root cause; all alternatives that assign the measured spans to test bodies or unavoidable fresh topology were rejected. Temporary DEBUG-rebar-debug instrumentation was removed and the worktree returned clean before Phase 2.

comments.body:
Phase 2 pre-repair review defect RCA (2026-08-14)

Problem: the new clone_topology_template helper remints .env-id and legacy .signing-key but leaves asymmetric .opcert-key/.opcert-key.pub copied verbatim.

Confirmed mechanism: tests/_topology_template.py:_IDENTITY_FILES and _remint_store_identities enumerate only .env-id and .signing-key. A runtime experiment initialized a real rebar store, generated its op-cert key through rebar.signing.ensure_opcert_key, cloned it twice through clone_topology_template, and compared SHA-256 digests without exposing key material. Template, clone A, and clone B all had the same private-key digest (77e03e4b35385449) and identical public-key bytes, while opcert_principal reported three distinct environment principals. This confirms that clones with distinct environment identity authenticate using one copied private key; the alternative that op-cert material was regenerated or omitted was rejected.

Defect legitimacy: this violates the ticket acceptance criterion that per-test copies cannot share environment IDs or signing keys and the helper's own contract that every rebar identity is reminted. The authoritative asymmetric key location and first-use generation contract are src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:28-30 and ensure_opcert_key at lines 152-186.

Caller-dependency sweep: the expected behavior is that copying a keyed template never copies private signing authority. clone_topology_template is used only by test fixture builders; no consumer relies on shared key bytes, and current optimized templates generally remain keyless. The safe behavior is to discard copied .opcert-key plus derivative .pub from each copied tracker, preserving lazy first-use generation. No behavioral dependency blocks repair.

Two consecutive successful macOS jobs identified exactly one phase over 20s: tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py::test_benchmark_commit_count_is_ceil_per_pass, 21.05s call in run 31854708530/job 94937320146 and 29.38s call in run 31854837190/job 94937686582. No instrumented fixture span exceeded 20s. The test imports 3,000 tickets plus 3,000 comments and asserts batched commit counts, making it an individual synthetic benchmark/long pole rather than ordinary unit behavior.

comments.body:
FINAL DEBUG / COMPLETION REPORT (2026-08-14)

Problem: five invariant Git/rebar fixture topologies were rebuilt from scratch for every consumer, contributing 103.416 measured worker-seconds across the top five modules in organic Verify run 31846417650.

Proven root cause: the function-scoped builders in test_secret_screen_e7a9.py, test_list_filters.py, test_concurrency_regression.py/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py, test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py, and test_inline_write_push.py performed repeated repository initialization and fixed topology population even though each asserted behavior begins from an equivalent post-setup state. Focused runtime probes separated setup from call work and measured real-build versus isolated-copy ratios of approximately 12x, 17.7x, 23x, 13.8x, and 15.7x.

Proof and OSS legitimacy: runtime mutation/isolation probes rejected test-body cost and unavoidable fresh-state semantics. Django setUpTestData/deep-copy plus rollback, Rails fixture loading plus rollback/cache invalidation, GitLab let_it_be/prepared repositories plus rollback/reload, and pytest tmp_path_factory all use the same expensive-template plus per-test-isolation practice, while retaining from-scratch cases where copying is not faithful. Tracker precedents peculiar-calmy-bubblefish and adored-duskish-kissingbug accepted and hardened this pattern; no rejection was found.

Tests and repair proof: commit 3bf9b2b2c41f00f76ee4c5298e185ab95e4269fb added/extended behavioral sentinels in tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py and migrated only proven-equivalent fixtures. The op-cert key defect was observed RED with identical template/A/B private-key digests, GREEN after copied .opcert-key/.pub removal and lazy reminting, and RED again when the exact defect was reintroduced. The object-alternates sentinel was RED before the fail-fast guard and GREEN afterward. Existing sentinels cover half-rewritten and bare worktree pointers, source-path leakage, shared refs/object stores, identity/signing isolation, restrictive key mode, virgin templates, sibling remotes, gate snapshots, caches, and mutable config. They assert observable Git/rebar behavior, not implementation text.

Fix: each pytest worker now builds five invariant templates once, then makes and repairs a complete isolated copy per test. Direct initialization/recovery contracts remain from-scratch. No production behavior or dependency changed. No test, assertion, selector, mutation shard, Python cell, or platform was removed, skipped, sampled, xfailed, or weakened. The merged diff added 591 lines and removed 103, predominantly reusable topology repair plus isolation contracts.

Scope and safety: all 125 affected tests passed in 46.95s. The exact local default selector passed 13,441 tests with 17 expected skips in 1,254.00s; the exact integration selector passed 167 with 2 skips in 114.59s. make check passed Ruff, format, complexity, DCO, workflow guards, and mypy. The local selectors used pytest automatic basetemps (no --basetemp override); their numbered temporary roots were not logged and were later pruned, so no retained-size claim is made.

Original-report replication: Gerrit 1799 patchset 1 passed LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 and merged as 3bf9b2b2c4. Its macOS log contained zero >1s fixture_setup spans from the five migrated modules; the previous organic run measured 103.416s in those modules. The only individual test above 20s was the separately owned 3,000-ticket/3,000-comment import benchmark at 21.05s. This proves the targeted repeated-setup mechanism is gone without claiming that all suite growth is solved.

CI_RESULT: {"run_id":"31854708530","status":"passed","duration":1857,"fixes_applied":[],"retry_count":0}. End-to-end was 30m57s; macOS was 29m22s, comprising 25m30s default, 2m04s integration, and 1m48s setup/teardown. Ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 jobs were 8m53s/9m59s/11m42s. The preceding organic run 31846417650 was 29m47s end-to-end, so this single noisy full-run pair does not demonstrate a wall-clock reduction; the causal evidence is the paired setup probes and disappearance of the targeted >1s spans. Fresh runs must determine the average.

Siblings: the five confirmed equivalent fixture families were repaired in scope. Initialization/recovery fixtures were intentionally excluded. No missing parallel surface exists because clone_topology_template is test infrastructure consumed only by these fixtures.

Residual risk and prevention: the import benchmark remains an individual contention long pole under ravenous-beribboned-walleye; its standalone behavior and accepted 3,000-record contract are not weakened here. A local 87.27s bare-pytest import-convention outlier reproduced standalone in 4.23s, classifying it as contention rather than intrinsic test work. Continued post-merge sampling is required before declaring the 20-30 minute average goal achieved.

Back-out: revert 3bf9b2b2c4 to restore per-test from-scratch fixture construction; no production behavior or coverage destination depends on the optimization.

## Context
Organic Gerrit Verify run 31846417650 emitted 260 fixture_setup spans over 1 second totaling 380.393 aggregate worker-seconds. Excluding the separately proven 35-second editor DNS delay, the largest module totals were: tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py 28.998s / 23 setups; tests/interfaces/queries/test_list_filters.py 25.856s / 17; tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py 19.230s / 7; tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py 16.486s / 11; and tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py 12.846s / 9. Closed precedent peculiar-calmy-bubblefish proved that a session template plus isolated per-test copies reduced tests/interfaces wall time from 270.7s to 186.5s (31%) while running nine more tests, and explicitly deferred roughly 20 module-local fixtures as the larger remaining win.

## Phase 1 plan
- Trace each measured >1s setup to its exact fixture and separate from-scratch git/rebar store initialization, fixture copying/fix-up, test-body work, and runner variance with setup-only timing plus runtime instrumentation.
- Test the dynamic hypothesis that the five modules repeatedly build equivalent virgin git-backed stores. Confirm only where the same initialized precondition recurs; reject template reuse for fixtures whose setup semantics intentionally vary or whose contract is initialization itself.
- Search ticket history for prior acceptance/rejection and compare the remediation with at least three popular, actively maintained OSS projects using session-scoped expensive templates with isolated per-test copy/reset. Apply the parent ticket consensus rule: at least two-thirds use the practice and none documents rejecting it for coverage/reliability.

## Phase 2 plan (only after confirmed RCA and consensus)
- Add or extend one uniquely named test helper at an existing call-graph seam; use session/worker-local templates and per-test copies only for confirmed equivalent fixtures.
- Preserve the safety contracts established by peculiar-calmy-bubblefish: rewrite both linked-worktree pointers, reject bare git worktree repair, allocate a per-test gate snapshot directory, regenerate environment/signing identity, reset module caches, keep the template virgin, and retain deliberate from-scratch initialization/recovery tests.
- Prove RED->GREEN with durable isolation sentinels before migrating consumers. Do not remove, skip, sample, xfail, or weaken any behavioral assertion.
- Run every affected module, full owning tiers, the full default/integration selectors, lint, typecheck, and workflow guards. Measure paired before/after setup and wall time under the same environment and report runner-seconds saved without claiming critical-path savings from aggregate fixture time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every targeted setup is attributed to a specific fixture operation with a focused measured baseline.
- [x] The confirmed RCA includes a runtime experiment that discriminates repeated equivalent store construction from test-body work and unavoidable per-test semantics.
- [x] Tracker history and at least three popular actively maintained OSS projects are cited; consensus is evaluated by the parent rule.
- [x] Only fixtures proven equivalent are migrated; initialization/recovery contracts continue to build from scratch.
- [x] Collected/passed test counts and all pre-existing assertions are preserved or increased.
- [x] Per-test copies cannot share ticket refs, linked-worktree paths, gate snapshots, environment IDs, signing keys, module caches, or mutable config state.
- [x] Durable sentinels fail for stale half-rewritten pointers, bare worktree repair, shared refs, shared identity/signing state, and non-virgin templates.
- [x] A defect-seeded mutation of each newly relied-on isolation fix returns the relevant sentinel to RED.
- [x] Paired before/after setup and module/tier wall-time measurements quantify runner-seconds saved.
- [x] Full affected tiers plus default/integration selectors, lint, typecheck, and workflow guards pass.
- [x] The Gerrit change receives LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 and merges before closure.

## Back-out
Revert the Gerrit change to restore per-test from-scratch fixture construction; no product behavior or coverage destination changes.
